# chinese-history

> Open structured database of Chinese history: 370 persons, 154 events, 551 reign eras, 49 dynasties, 62 museum-held artifacts — 1224 records. JSON distribution (clone-and-use) plus a single-file SQLite build. Every record carries `sources`. Inspired by chinese-poetry.

Repo: https://github.com/anthonyhann/chinese-history
Discussions: https://github.com/anthonyhann/chinese-history/discussions
Issues: https://github.com/anthonyhann/chinese-history/issues

## Where to get it

- Clone: `git clone https://github.com/anthonyhann/chinese-history.git`
- Single-file SQLite (1.8 MB, 10 tables): latest GitHub Release, or build with `python3 tools/build_sqlite.py`
- JSON snapshot zip: latest GitHub Release
- Verified entry point: run `python3 tools/validate.py` first — it prints the record count and fails on any inconsistency

## Repo layout

- `persons/{dynasty}/person.{dynasty}.{n}.json` — persons, ≤1000 records per shard
- `events/{dynasty}/event.{dynasty}.{n}.json` — events
- `artifacts/{dynasty}/artifact.{dynasty}.{n}.json` — artifacts (museum-held Chinese cultural relics)
- `dynasties/dynasties.json` — dynasty base table (id, name, start/end year, capital)
- `reign_eras/{dynasty}.json` — era-name → Gregorian year mapping table
- `places/places.json` — historical place → modern name + coordinates
- `museums/museums.json` — holding institutions + their open-data license status
- `schema/*.schema.json` — human-readable JSON Schema contracts
- `tools/validate.py` — zero-dependency validator (stdlib only): JSON parse, required fields, id rules, mandatory sources, referential integrity, artifact image license rules
- `tools/build_sqlite.py` — builds the single-file SQLite database from the JSON shards

## Entity id conventions

- Format: `entity.domain.slug`, lowercase, e.g. `person.qin.yingzheng`, `dynasty.han`, `event.qin.shaqiu-bian`
- Ids are frozen once published and never reused
- Cross-references: `person.events[]`, `event.participants[].person`, `artifact.current_holder.museum`, `person.predecessor/successor`

## Time representation (dual-track)

- `year` / `start` / `end`: integer Gregorian year; **negative = BC** (`-221` = 221 BC)
- `original`: original Chinese historical notation (e.g. "秦始皇三十七年七月丙寅")
- `circa: true` = approximate; `disputed[]` = competing scholarly values, each with its own source
- Era names are **not unique across polities**: 贞观 is both Tang 627–649 and Western Xia 1101–1113. Always resolve an era name together with its `dynasty`.
- `person.reign.start` may precede accession as emperor (e.g. 秦始皇 `reign.start = -247` is accession as King of Qin, not -221 when he took the imperial title). Read `reign.note`.
- Dynasty ids are not always the modern shorthand: Western Xia is `dynasty.western-xia`.

## Licensing

- Code: MIT. Facts: CC0. Original descriptive text: CC BY-SA 4.0. Artifact images: per-record `images[].license`; non-CC0 images are `link`-only, never hotlinked.

## Data status & contributing

- Records are AI-pipeline generated (`_meta.created_by`, `_meta.model`, `_meta.prompt_version`). `_meta` provides traceability, **not a correctness guarantee**.
- **No record has been individually human-verified yet.** There is no `verified_by` field in `_meta`; that was documented previously but was never implemented.
- `sources` is mandatory and CI-enforced, but the validator only checks that `sources` is present and well-formed — it cannot verify that the cited book actually says this. Cross-check before citing in production.
- Known gap: `disputed[]` competing values are populated for only 9 of 370 persons.
- Corrections must cite sources; run `python3 tools/validate.py` before submitting
- Contributing guide: `CONTRIBUTING.md` (Chinese). Code of conduct: `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`.
- For questions, design discussion, or "what did you build with this", use Discussions rather than Issues
